items.headline: Sound Transit Board Confirms $34.5B Gap — Ballard Link Market Street Extension 'Not Currently Affordable'; ST3 Restructured; West Seattle Link Continues; Longview CSB Day 8; Unstable Tank Ongoing
items.summary: Two major infrastructure development items on June 2 morning. First: Sound Transit's governing board voted to approve a sweeping overhaul of the voter-approved ST3 expansion plan, acknowledging a $34.5 billion funding gap — one of the largest unfunded regional transit obligations in the western United States. The agency cites rising construction costs, inflation, lower-than-expected revenues, and increasing operating expenses. Key restructuring: the Ballard Link Extension from Seattle Center to Market Street is 'not currently affordable' and requires additional funding before construction can proceed. Only the initial Ballard Link segment to Seattle Center is fully funded under the revised plan. The West Seattle Link Extension remains funded (Avalon Station removed). Tacoma and West Seattle extensions move forward. Additional revenue measures under exploration: fare gates, Washington Clean Fuels Standard carbon credit program, other operational changes. The $34.5B gap reshapes the regional transit expansion Puget Sound voters approved in 2016 — Ballard voters face an indefinite wait for the full extension to Market Street. Second: Longview Nippon Dynawave paper mill CSB investigation advances to Day 8. All 11 victims recovered and identified. Approximately 90,000 gallons of white liquor in the structurally unstable tank; Columbia River contamination assessment ongoing; EPA Region 10 and WA Department of Ecology monitoring active. The OPB pre-warning regulatory thread — March 2026 workers notified WA DOLI of sinkhole at implosion site — continues to define the investigation's fact pattern and regulatory liability arc.
